Hi, I wrote about this in this list a bit earlier.

The solution proposed in the single responce you have received before
mine is a solution to a different problem.

What I had to do was - recompile the package without using the rules for
building package in ubuntu.

That is dirty, I know, but that was the best I could do...

Here is what you have to do:

# install the rkward build dependencies
sudo apt-get build-dep rkward
# remove the damaged rkward
sudo apt-get remove rkward
## do not remove the packages that apt-get will suggest to remove after this
# get the sources of rkward - regular download, or the debian way:
apt-get source rkward
#now, go into rkward-* directory, find the INSTALL or README file and
follow the prescribed procedure to build and install the package..

After that you might still have to deal with the missing plugins
problem: see the thread proposed to you earlier.

Donatas

messages.body_plain:
Am Dienstag 04 November 2008 20:39:35 schrieb Donatas G.:
> What I had to do was - recompile the package without using the rules for
> building package in ubuntu.
>
> That is dirty, I know, but that was the best I could do...

i've managed to find the showstopper in the debian/rules -- two lines have to 
be altered. change line 37 from
    -DDATA_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/share/apps/ \
to
    -DDATA_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/share/kde4/apps \

and line 80 from
    rm -vf $(CURDIR)/debian/rkward/usr/share/apps/katepart/syntax/r.xml
to
    rm -vf $(CURDIR)/debian/rkward/usr/share/kde4/apps/katepart/syntax/r.xml

if needed, apply the Rdevices.h patch (i.e. remove its inclusion as described 
by thomas). afterwards, building a functional debian package with
   fakeroot dpkg-buildpackage -uc -us
   sudo dpkg -i ../rkward_0.5.0b-2_i386.deb
worked for me.

you may have to correct the path to all.pluginmap (rkward configuration -> 
plug-ins) as well, which is now to be found in /usr/share/kde4/apps/rkward/, 
of course.

most icons still seem to be out of path, though. but apart from that, rkward 
is fully functional.

hallo ,

am Montag, 17. November 2008 (20:48) schrieb Prasenjit Kapat:
> Is this only for Hardy or Intrepid or both?

that's for intrepid.

i've built a package from the same sources on a hardy system as well. but 
intrepid installs kde4 as default (prefix is /usr), whereas hardy comes with 
kde3 and the ability to install kde4 as well. all kde4 stuff in hardy is 
therefor installed (aka prefix) to /usr/lib/kde4, with e.g. the 
data_install_dir then being /usr/lib/kde4/share/kde4/apps. [i'm serious...]

so, just alter the paths in the rules file depending on your kubuntu version 
and you should be fine. on hardy, you might have to "export 
PATH=$PATH:/usr/lib/kde4/bin" before calling dpkg-buildpackage, otherwise 
kde4 won't be found.

Am Dienstag 18 November 2008 00:06:29 schrieb Prasenjit Kapat:
> :)) Hmmm... ?But, why is intrepid using /usr/share/kde4/apps instead

i agree. in fact, it does use /usr/share/apps as well. but perhaps its a 
transitional state, and they're trying to clean up the directory tree... i'm 
not an kubuntu developer, so i have no insight in that.

you can use the kde4-config command to get information about verious expected 
paths. for instance, to find the path for the data_install_dir:
 kde4-config --path data

("kde4-config --types" will list all available types).

> Anyway, it is good to know this non-trivial convention!!

to me it seemed the obvious place to look: if cmake/make/make install works, 
but debian/rules doesn't, i guessed that the cmake call in the rules file with 
its list of options was to blame. i removed all options, as expected the 
package worked, after that i just rebuild the package with more and more 
options until the errors reoccurred: gotcha ;-)

> Thanks, I'll try that sometime. I am still using Hardy and I've pinned
> R at 2.7.2... I just didn't want to break the current (working!)
> setup...

wisely so... however, this path issues are unrelated to the Rdevices.h issue 
with R 2.8. you could try to compile against 2.7 first, and if it doesn't work 
for you, simply re-install the official package.

Read and respond to this message at: https://sourceforge.net/forum/message.php?msg_id=5688330 By: fsando Hi What I'm going to suggest is more of a hack but I think it points the way to a long term solution. In rkward graphs are made through a call to the function rk.graph.on() This function creates graph images in the ~/.rkward folder. It automatically names graph.01.png, graph.02.png etc. (or something very similar) When I make graphs now I always write code like this rk.graph.on() plot(x,y....) rk.grahp.off() The image is not actually created until rk.graph.off() is run. ", sep = ""), file = rk.get.output.html.file(), append = TRUE) } It is called like this a3q_rk.graph.on(width,height,graph_name) plot(x,y....) rk.grahp.off() ______________________________________________________________________ You are receiving this email because you elected to monitor this forum.
